key_insight: The paper introduces a hardware-efficient variational quantum ansatz whose Fubini-Study metric is exactly diagonal in closed form, enabling metric-aware optimization, time evolution, and Haar sampling without auxiliary metric circuits or matrix inversion.
engineering_relevance: This can substantially reduce two-qubit gate counts and calibration overhead in quantum simulation workflows, while also enabling spin-adapted circuit designs with exact symmetry control.
method: Binary-tree parameterized ansatz with closed-form diagonal pullback metric
Pruning compiler exploits gauge freedom when the target lives in a sparse computational-basis subspace
Interchangeable Schur-transform dressing or internal reparameterizations enforce exact spin adaptation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reference-level accuracy on small-molecule electronic structure and half-filled Hubbard quench dynamics using one to three orders of magnitude fewer two-qubit gates than leading alternatives.
watch_item: The bare ansatz is classically simulable in the sparse-subspace size k, so practical advantage depends on the chosen dressing/composition and on managing compilation complexity for larger systems.
paper_title: A hardware-efficient variational ansatz with an exact diagonal metric for real- and imaginary-time evolution and Haar sampling
